question.text: The final settlement price for exchange-traded currency options is:

answer.text: The applicable FBIL reference rate(s) on the last trading day
The last traded premium of the option
The average spot rate of the last week

explanation.text: The Logic: Final settlement of exchange-traded currency options uses the applicable FBIL reference rate(s) on the last trading day. For INR currency options, this is the FBIL reference rate for the relevant INR pair; for cross-currency options, final settlement is computed using the applicable FBIL reference rates for USD-INR, EUR-INR, GBP-INR and JPY-INR on the last trading day. The Trap: The option's final settlement is based on the underlying's reference rate(s), not on the option's own last traded price. Note: Page 88 of the NISM Series-I workbook lists the final settlement price as the FBIL reference rate on the last trading day for INR currency options; pages 89 and 166 specify the applicable FBIL reference rates for cross-currency option settlement.
